name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the freshest AI-news feeds from the last 24 h: run `curl -s https://feeds.bloomberg.com/technology/feed.xml | xq '.rss.channel.item | length'` to count Bloomberg AI items, then `curl -s https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/news/ | pup 'h2' | wc -l` to tally NVIDIA AI headlines. I’ll save raw XML/HTML to `/tmp/ai-news-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).{xml,html}` and log the counts in `/tmp/ai-news-counts.log`.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Hold on—your Bloomberg feed check is a *length count* on raw XML, not a filtered AI-item tally. That risks conflating AI with general tech noise. And your NVIDIA scrape uses `pup 'h2'`—but NVIDIA’s news page buries AI headlines under "Press Releases" or "Blogs," not just `<h2>` tags. Where’s the validation that these selectors actually capture *AI-specific* content? Show me the filtered output, not just the raw counts.

name: Scoop
text:
Scoop (news-w2): I’ll fix the noise: first, pull Bloomberg’s AI-only RSS via `curl -s https://feeds.bloomberg.com/technology/feed.xml | xq '.rss.channel.item[] | select(.title | ascii_downcase | contains("ai") or contains("artificial intelligence")) | length'` to get a clean AI-item count. Then, for NVIDIA, I’ll scrape the Press Releases page directly with `curl -s https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/press-release | pup 'h3' text{}' | grep -i "ai\|artificial intelligence" | wc -l` to tally only AI-focused headlines. Files: `bloomberg_ai_count.json` and `nvidia_ai_headlines.txt` will store raw outputs for audit.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** Your Bloomberg filter still risks *false positives*—"AI" appears in job titles ("AI Engineer") or tangential mentions ("AI-driven markets") that aren’t *news* about AI advancements. And your NVIDIA scrape ignores dynamic content: if their page loads AI headlines via JavaScript (e.g., React), `pup` will return zero. Where’s the evidence that static scraping captures their full feed? Provide a `curl` + `grep` fallback or API endpoint proof.

name: Wire
text:
DECISION: Use Bloomberg’s AI-specific RSS feed + NVIDIA’s sitemap API for static AI headlines; exclude dynamic JS content.

Artifact must contain:
- Bloomberg AI-item count (filtered, no false positives)
- NVIDIA AI-headline tally (static only)
- Timestamp + source URLs
